hypothesis: In mm/swapfile.c, cluster_alloc_swap_entry() and swap_alloc_fast() acquire spinlocks (ci->lock and si->lock) for every single page allocation. Reserving a batch of contiguous swap slots (e.g. 16 to 64 entries) per-CPU in percpu_swap_cluster amortizes lock acquisition, atomic accounting, and cluster scanning over the batch while safely releasing any unallocated slots on flush/swapoff, reducing swapout latency without wasting unallocated slots. Reject if candidate leaks swap slots, corrupts swap cache, fails correctness gates, or fails calibrated screening.

mechanism.claim: In mm/swapfile.c, percpu_swap_cluster maintains an order-0 batched swap slot reservation, refilling up to 32 contiguous entries under ci->lock with a single swap_range_alloc() update and serving subsequent order-0 allocations directly without redundant spinlock contention or list manipulations, releasing unused slots on device flush.
mechanism.falsifier: Exact-tree review shows lost lifetime protection, incorrect slot conflict handling, or broken cache lookup fallback. Correctness, metadata spread <1%, and calibrated fast-tier screen independently gate execution.
